findings.observation: Reviewed site plan sheets (Sheets 1, 8-9, 13-15) and planting/hardscape plans (Sheets 46, 51). No tower crane is shown or referenced anywhere in the plan set. The consolidated site plan application (Property Attributes section) indicates 'Will a License Agreement Application be submitted for this project? No' - suggesting no License Agreements are being pursued, which would include tower cranes.
findings.reasoning: A tower crane would be prominently shown on site plans and demolition plans, especially for a 6-story building construction project. The absence of any tower crane symbols, notes, or License Agreement references throughout the plan set confirms that no tower crane is proposed. The condition 'If tower crane proposed' is not met.
findings.explanation: No tower crane is proposed for this project.

findings.observation: Examined excavation and construction-related sheets including Existing Conditions & Demolition Plans (Sheets 8-9), Grading Plans (Sheets 21-22), and utility plans (Sheets 18-20, 25). No retention systems, shoring, or excavation support structures are shown extending into public right-of-way. All excavation work appears to be within the property limits.
findings.reasoning: Retention or excavation support systems in ROW would be shown on grading, demolition, or utility plans with specific callouts and details. The absence of any such systems in the ROW, combined with the application statement that no License Agreement will be submitted, confirms this condition is not met.
findings.explanation: No retention or excavation support systems in ROW are proposed.

findings.observation: Reviewed Hardscape Plan (Sheet 46) which includes a Material Schedule listing bike racks (7.2) and potentially other streetscape elements. Vision analysis of Sheet 46 confirmed that while bike racks are listed in the schedule, there are no clear callouts placing them in the public ROW - they appear to be on private property. No awnings, canopies, benches, or trash receptacles are shown in the ROW.
findings.reasoning: The Material Schedule lists bike racks, but the vision analysis could not identify any '7.2' callouts in the ROW area. The Hardscape Plan shows improvements in ROW (sidewalks, trees) but the specific streetscape furniture elements listed in this checklist item either don't appear or are located on private property. Since these elements are not clearly shown in ROW, no License Agreement is required for them.
findings.explanation: No streetscape elements (awnings, canopies, benches, bike racks, trash receptacles) are clearly shown in ROW. Bike racks listed in material schedule appear to be on private property.

findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 51 (Planting Plan) clearly shows proposed street trees and landscaping outside the property line in the public ROW. The vision agent reported: 'Yes. There are extensive tree plantings shown outside the solid line defined as the PROPERTY LINE... They are located between the property line and the faint background lines that indicate the street curbs, which is standard for a public ROW.' Evenly spaced rows of proposed trees run along the northern, eastern, and southern street frontages, with stippled planting bed areas. The Limit of Construction (LOC) extends into ROW to encompass these landscape elements. However, the Consolidated Site Plan Application (Property Attributes section) states: 'Will a License Agreement Application be submitted for this project? [ ] Yes (x) No' - the No box is checked. No License Agreement document is included in the supplementary documents, and no License Agreement reference appears on the plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: Street trees and landscaping in public ROW require a License Agreement per Austin regulations. The plans clearly show these improvements in ROW, but the application explicitly states no License Agreement will be submitted, no License Agreement document is in the submittal, and no License Agreement is referenced on the plans. This is a deficiency - the required License Agreement application is not submitted or referenced despite the plans showing improvements that require it.
findings.explanation: Street trees and landscaping are shown in ROW on Sheet 51, but no License Agreement for these improvements is submitted or referenced. Application states no License Agreement will be submitted.
findings.resolution: Submit License Agreement application for street trees, landscaping, and irrigation in public right-of-way as shown on Sheet 51 (Planting Plan), or reference the submitted application on the plan sheets.

Without definitive labels showing street lights in the ROW, their location cannot be confirmed.

The grouping requires a License Agreement specifically 'If pedestrian lighting in ROW' - without clear evidence that proposed pedestrian lighting is in ROW, the condition is not met. The ambiguity favors the applicant in a completeness check.

findings.observation: This is a catch-all item for any required License or Encroachment Agreement. Based on evaluation of CC-24-01 through CC-24-06, street trees and landscaping in ROW (CC-24-04) require a License Agreement. However, the Consolidated Site Plan Application states 'Will a License Agreement Application be submitted for this project? No'. No License Agreement documents are included in the supplementary documents, and no License Agreement references appear on the plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: Since CC-24-04 identified that street trees and landscaping are proposed in ROW (which require a License Agreement), this catch-all item captures that same deficiency. The required License Agreement application is not submitted or referenced on plans. This item serves as a backup check to ensure no required agreements are missed.

findings.resolution: Submit License Agreement application for improvements in public right-of-way, specifically for street trees and landscaping shown on Sheet 51.

findings.observation: Sheet 6 (General Notes - Austin Water Information) includes an 'ADDITIONAL REVIEW ACKNOWLEDGEMENT' section with an 'AULCC REQUIREMENT' subsection. The form asks 'DOES THIS PROJECT REQUIRE AULCC REVIEW? (>300 LF OF W/WW PIPING IN ROW)' and the YES checkbox is filled. The form then states 'IF YES, PLEASE PROVIDE UCC#' with the response '(pending)'. The site is not in the Downtown Austin Project Coordination Zone (DAPCZ) per facts.md, so the threshold is 300 LF outside DAPCZ. The project acknowledges exceeding this threshold but has not provided the AULCC case number or completeness letter.
findings.reasoning: The plans explicitly acknowledge that AULCC review is required due to >300 LF of water/wastewater piping in ROW. However, the AULCC case number (UCC#) is listed as 'pending', which means the AULCC Completeness Letter has not been obtained and the case number is not provided. Per the checklist item, plans must be 'submitted or referenced for AULCC' when excavations exceed thresholds - marking the case number as pending without providing documentation is a completeness deficiency.
findings.explanation: AULCC review required (>300 LF W/WW in ROW confirmed on Sheet 6), but AULCC case number is listed as 'pending' - no case number or completeness letter provided.
findings.resolution: Obtain AULCC case number and Completeness Letter, then update Sheet 6 with the actual UCC# and reference the AULCC coordination documentation in the submittal.

findings.observation: This item requires AULCC coordination when a License Agreement or tower crane is involved. No tower crane is proposed (see CC-24-01). However, street trees and landscaping in ROW are shown on Sheet 51, which require a License Agreement per CC-24-04. Although the applicant states no License Agreement will be submitted, the improvements requiring a License Agreement ARE shown on the plans, which means 'License Agreement is involved' for purposes of triggering AULCC. Sheet 6 confirms AULCC is required and the UCC# is 'pending' - no AULCC case number or completeness letter provided.
findings.reasoning: The condition 'If License Agreement or tower crane' means if improvements requiring a License Agreement are proposed OR if a tower crane is proposed. Since street trees/landscaping requiring a License Agreement are shown in ROW (even though the application incorrectly states no License Agreement will be submitted), this triggers the AULCC requirement. This is an independent trigger from CC-24-15 (though both apply to this project). The AULCC documentation is not provided - case number is pending.
findings.explanation: AULCC required due to License Agreement-triggering improvements (street trees/landscaping in ROW), but AULCC case number is 'pending' - no case number or completeness letter provided.
findings.resolution: Obtain AULCC case number and Completeness Letter, then update Sheet 6 with the actual UCC# and reference the AULCC coordination documentation in the submittal.
